MCCHEAM212.contribution: studies Renaissance Italy in connection with Islamic Eastern Mediterranean courts and other trading and artistic networks
MCCHEAM212.topics: This course examines the painting, sculpture, and architecture of Renaissance Italy and the extensive artistic connections that linked the Italian peninsula to other regions of the world. By exploring a range of geographical contexts, from the Islamic courts of the Eastern Mediterranean and the commercial routes connecting Europe, Asia, and Africa to the newly encountered territories of the Americas, students will examine how trade, colonization, and cross-cultural exchange shaped the production and meaning of Renaissance art.

MCCHEAM316.contribution: develops research and writing about art through critical interpretation of images and sources
MCCHEAM316.topics: This course examines the history of art history as an academic discipline, tracing how scholars have understood and interpreted art from the sixteenth century to the present. Through critical readings of influential texts by figures such as Aby Warburg, Erwin Panofsky, Ernst Gombrich, Michel Foucault, and Jacques Derrida, students explore the major ideas and methodologies that have shaped the field. Topics include art and history, aesthetics, meaning and interpretation, authorship and identity, and the challenges of art history in a globalized world.

candidateAssessment.concept: Comparative History, Conflict and Middle East–Europe Relations
candidateAssessment.assessment: The strongest trial combines empire, Mediterranean connections, Arabic and Near Eastern narratives, conflict, EU politics and international relations. Ancient Persia and Renaissance Mediterranean exchange contribute real regional content, but the plan does not sustain modern Middle Eastern history, politics or region-specific methods. General conflict and international relations cannot supply the missing regional inquiry.

The strongest cultural materials are Eastern Mediterranean artistic exchange and Arabic literary examples. Media, life writing and sociology support comparative interpretation but do not establish sustained study of modern Middle Eastern societies, migration and soft power.

Arabic narratives appear in translation and do not establish a regional source-based course sequence. This candidate lacks a sustained area-studies focus independently of the absence of language acquisition or a study-abroad placement.

candidateAssessment.concept: Religion and Diversity in the Middle East
candidateAssessment.assessment: Islamic courts and Arabic narratives contribute cultural examples. The workbook does not establish sustained study of Judaism and Islam as traditions or of their relationships with political life and social diversity in the region.

academicFinding: UCR offers related study of empires, Mediterranean exchange, literature and international relations. Even when combined in a feasible programme, these courses do not provide sustained study of modern Middle Eastern societies, politics and religious traditions or the regional methods needed to connect those subjects. These are central to Groningen’s degree.
